A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamCAD and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and separate supplement numbering in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original multimodal reconstruction experiments, caption evaluations, user studies, ablations, and topology-recovery results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and additionally supplies DeepCAD comparison scores, surface-extraction and perturbation experiments, and failure examples.

M1.justification: The shared-boundary Bézier VAE, coarse-to-fine flow generation, Stable Diffusion text-to-image stage, and Qwen3 topology-recovery approach remain unchanged. V2 adds tests and implementation disclosures without establishing a revision to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The ten-source training corpus, three input modalities, and ABC/Objaverse coverage are retained. DeepCAD already appears in v1's baseline training and announced supplementary comparison; v2 supplies its missing results. Perturbations of internal surfaces and voxels introduce diagnostic protocols within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Section 5.3 newly evaluates an SDF-based surface-extraction alternative against the proposed flood-fill initialization. The named comparator sets in the corresponding ABC/Objaverse experiments remain unchanged; the DeepCAD table uses existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces protocols comparing flood-fill and SDF VAEs trained on 100K samples and testing Gaussian perturbations of initial surfaces and coarse voxels on 15K ABC samples. It also removes Invalidity Ratio from the main evaluation metrics. Existing main training budgets, splits, and geometric sampling procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds surface-extraction comparison, initialization sensitivity, and coarse-stage sensitivity experiments, plus explicit failure cases. These examine previously untested pipeline dependencies beyond v1's regularization, resolution, metadata, and diffusion fine-tuning ablations. Main and supplementary Table 4 repeat the same perturbation analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's Gaussian noise levels specify sensitivity-test conditions, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds DeepCAD results, including DreamCAD point-to-CAD F1 of 94.91 and CD of 0.12 × 10^-3, alongside extraction and perturbation findings. All retained main Table 2 values are unchanged, but 34 invalidity-rate entries disappear. V2 newly attributes a 62% CD reduction to comparison with NURBGen, although the listed values, 20.32 versus 50.84, imply approximately 60%.

T1.justification: The rational Bézier definition, differentiable tessellation, shared-boundary construction, and mathematical objectives remain equivalent. V2 adds no theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: The annotation-free scaling, CADCap-1M, and multimodal performance contributions remain. V2 shifts the abstract's editable STEP claim from the generated surfaces to downstream topology recovery, removes the introduction's direct-export/editability passage, and drops 'editable' from the conclusion's description of base outputs.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting SDF extraction to smoothing, perturbation sensitivity to dependence on accurate initialization and coarse geometry, and missing small holes to voxel resolution. It interprets the DeepCAD comparison as evidence beyond data scale. The existing limitation concerning incomplete CAD topology remains.

D1.justification: The supplement newly documents the existing topology experiment's ABC sampling, 10K-token filtering, 2,000-epoch patch optimization at learning rate 10^-4, and three Qwen3 fine-tuning epochs with a 20K context window. It also specifies DeepCAD training from scratch and same-data baseline selection. V1's direct OpenCascade STEP-export disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: The OpenCascade software reference, v1 reference 44, is removed. The substantive related-work discussion and remaining cited research are retained after citation reordering and bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: Existing prose receives localized edits in the abstract, introduction, results, and conclusion. V2 expands supplementary explanations, adjusts headings and numbering, and adds keywords and corresponding-author information. Most original wording and narrative order remain.

P2.justification: The manuscript changes from two-column to narrow single-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. V2 merges the metadata and diffusion illustrations, expands Figure 4 from four caption examples to six, removes Table 2's invalidity columns, and adds DeepCAD, perturbation, and failure-case displays. Most existing qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The supplied DeepCAD comparison addresses the data-scale confound acknowledged but unsupported by results in v1. New diagnostic experiments, failure analysis, and topology-training details improve experimental support and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of comparative invalidity rates and the new mismatch between the claimed 62% reduction against NURBGen and Table 2's approximately 60%, supporting a limited overall improvement.
